text: So how did a scrape open up so much of the hull? Researchers point to the rivets. The Titanic's plates were held together by about three million rivets. Along the middle of the ship, hydraulic machines pressed in strong steel rivets. But at the curved bow and stern, the machines couldn't fit. Workers hammered in wrought iron rivets by hand. Rivets recovered from the wreck held a lot of slag, the glassy leftovers of iron-making, which can make rivets weaker and more brittle. When the iceberg shoved the plates, rivet heads could snap off. The seams opened, and the sea poured in.
